newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian economy to grow 3.0 pct - Access.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian economy to grow 3.0 pct - Access.

text.p: Economic forecaster Access Economics said on Monday it expected the Australian economy to grow 3.0 percent in fiscal 1996/97 ending June 30 from the previous year, below the budget forecast for growth of 3.5 percent.

Access said short term negatives for growth included the continued rise in stock accumulation, signs of a mild slowdown in the Asian Tiger economies and a slightly slower than expected upturn in the housing market.
"We are now less dogmatic in our views as to the timing of the next upturn," Access said in its December quarter report.
"We still have output growth strengthening again from the June quarter 1997, but a delay of one or two quarters in the next upswing would not surprise," Access said.
It said unemployment was now likely to peak at 8.9 percent in mid-1997 before improving slowly as a result of strengthening output across the economy during 1997/98.
"As we have said for some time, unemployment will rise slightly through to early 1997, reaching 8.9 percent at that time.
"It is projected to fall back in late 1997, as the output recovery starts to reach the labour market, and to continue to fall well into 1998."
Access said it expected headline inflation to fall to a year average 1.6 percent in the 1996/97 year, compared with the government's forecast of 2.0 percent.
The group revised its previous forecast for inflation of 2.1 percent to reflect its belief that there would be a further cut in interest rates early in 1997 and the strength of the Australian dollar.
But it warned that headline inflation may again break through 3.0 percent by the second half of calendar 1998 as economic activity, particularly in the housing market, picks up.
Headline inflation includes all consumer prices, including consumer interest charges and energy, which are excluded from the alternative underlying measure.
The report, written before the Reserve Bank made its surprise monetary easing on Wednesday, said there would be another 50-basis-point interest rate cut in February.
Access had expected that cut to be the last in the current cycle. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
